# Recommended Recipe

Source: https://autoarm.rhizomatics.org.uk/configuration/examples/recommended_recipe/

A simple standard setup for a home that's lived in most days, with no YAML:

- **Armed night** for a fixed bedtime every day, from a [Times of the Day](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/tod/) sensor
- **Armed home** from sunset until bedtime, when sunset comes first
- **Disarmed** when bedtime ends, or **armed home** until sunrise if it's still dark
- **Armed away** whenever everyone is out
- A calendar for vacations and other planned time away, with no need to switch the bedtime sensor off for them
- Coming home on the last day of a vacation or time away ends it, without waiting for the calendar

## Set Up

1. Create a **Bedtime** sensor in **Settings** > **Devices & Services** > **Helpers** > **Create Helper** > **Times of the Day**, on at 23:00 and off at 07:00, or whatever suits.
1. Have a calendar for vacations and time away. If you don't have one, see [Create a Calendar](https://autoarm.rhizomatics.org.uk/configuration/create_calendar/index.md).
1. Add the integration from **Settings** > **Devices & Services** > **Add Integration**, searching for **Auto Arm**, or if it's already set up, open **Settings** > **Devices & Services** > **Auto Arm** > **Configure**:

| Setting                                          | Value                                                 |
| ------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| **Bedtime - Times of the Day Sensor**            | The Bedtime sensor                                    |
| **Occupancy - Calendars**                        | The calendar                                          |
| **Presence - People for Occupancy Based Arming** | Everyone who lives in, already chosen on a new set up |

Everything else is left at its default on a new set up.

If Auto Arm was already set up, its existing settings are kept, so also check these in the **Advanced - Diurnal** section:

| Setting                                        | Value      |
| ---------------------------------------------- | ---------- |
| **Occupied state between morning and evening** | Disarmed   |
| **Occupied state between bedtime and morning** | Armed Home |
| **Occupied state between evening and bedtime** | Armed Home |

## An Ordinary Day

With someone home, and sunset at 18:00:

| Time  | What happens       | Alarm state                                             |
| ----- | ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| 07:00 | Bedtime sensor off | `disarmed`, or `armed_home` until sunrise if still dark |
| 18:00 | Sunset             | `armed_home`                                            |
| 23:00 | Bedtime sensor on  | `armed_night`                                           |

In summer, sunrise comes during bedtime and is ignored. In winter, bedtime ends before sunrise, so the alarm goes to `armed_home` at 07:00 and is disarmed at sunrise. To disarm as bedtime ends whatever the sun is doing, set **Occupied state between bedtime and morning** to Disarmed. If sunset comes after bedtime has started, it's ignored too.

If everyone is out, the alarm is `armed_away` at any time of day. Coming home during bedtime sets it to `armed_night`.

## Vacations and Time Away

Add a calendar event with **Vacation** or **Away** in its title. While the event is live it takes priority over the Bedtime sensor, which carries on turning on and off with no effect.

Coming home on the day the event is due to end finishes it there and then, so there's no need to match the calendar to the exact time you get back. Coming home on any earlier day leaves the alarm armed, as does anyone who is always shown as home, for example without location sharing switched on. This is the **Coming home ends Away and Vacation events on their last day** switch, in the **Advanced - Occupancy** section, which is on by default.

When the event ends during bedtime, the alarm goes to `armed_night`, or stays `armed_away` until someone is home. When it ends at any other time, the alarm is armed away if nobody is home, otherwise disarmed during the day, or `armed_home` after sunset.

Sunset still arms the alarm on a day with one of these calendar events, once the event has ended. The sunset [trigger](https://autoarm.rhizomatics.org.uk/automated_arming/#triggers) is only off by default on days with a `disarmed`, `armed_home` or `armed_night` calendar event.

# Typical Configuration

Source: https://autoarm.rhizomatics.org.uk/configuration/examples/typical/

More extensive example configuration, using most of the features.

## UI vs YAML Settings

With the config flow, most settings are now managed in the UI:

| Setting                                   | Where                                                     | Notes                                                                                                                                                      |
| ----------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Alarm panel entity                        | UI (setup)                                                | Selected when adding the integration                                                                                                                       |
| Change state using panel actions          | UI (options, Advanced)                                    | On for new installs, see [Create Panel](https://autoarm.rhizomatics.org.uk/configuration/create_panel/index.md)                                            |
| Arm and explain by voice, Disarm by voice | UI (options)                                              | Voice and chat commands, see [Automated Arming](https://autoarm.rhizomatics.org.uk/automated_arming/#built-in-agent-sentences)                             |
| Bedtime sensor                            | UI (setup, options)                                       | Times of the Day sensor for `armed_night`, see [Recommended Recipe](https://autoarm.rhizomatics.org.uk/configuration/examples/recommended_recipe/index.md) |
| Calendar entities                         | UI (setup, options)                                       | Which calendars to use                                                                                                                                     |
| Person entities                           | UI (setup, options)                                       | Which persons to track for occupancy                                                                                                                       |
| Occupied states                           | UI (options, Advanced - Diurnal)                          | Alarm state when occupied by day, after bedtime and before bedtime                                                                                         |
| Times of the Day sensors                  | UI (options)                                              | Sensors that set any other alarm state while on                                                                                                            |
| Calendar end modes                        | UI (options, Advanced - Calendar)                         | What happens when an armed or disarmed calendar event ends                                                                                                 |
| Triggers                                  | UI (options, Advanced - Diurnal and Advanced - Occupancy) | Whether sunrise, sunset and people arriving or leaving re-evaluate the state                                                                               |
| Sunrise and sunset                        | UI (options)                                              | Earliest and latest times                                                                                                                                  |
| Calendar match rules                      | UI (options, Advanced - Calendar)                         | Regex patterns matching calendar events to alarm states, copied from YAML if already there                                                                 |
| Calendar poll interval                    | UI (options, Advanced - Calendar)                         | How often to check the calendars                                                                                                                           |
| Transitions                               | YAML                                                      | Condition templates for state transitions                                                                                                                  |
| Buttons                                   | UI (options, Buttons)                                     | Physical button entities and delays, copied from YAML if already there                                                                                     |
| Notifications                             | UI (options)                                              | Notification service and targets, and priorities for Supernotify                                                                                           |
| Notification Profiles                     | YAML                                                      | **Deprecated**, replaced by deeper Supernotify integration in the options, and will be removed when Home Assistant 2027.4 is released                      |
| Rate limit                                | YAML                                                      | Throttling for arm calls                                                                                                                                   |

## Full YAML Example

```yaml
autoarm:
  # MIGRATED delay_time is copied into the Options the first time, and set there from then on
  occupancy:
    delay_time:
      not_home: 180
      home: 0 # the default
  # YAML-only: transition conditions
  transitions:
    armed_home:
      alias: Home with alarm active, such as home alone
      conditions:
        - "{{ autoarm.occupied and not autoarm.night }}"
        - "{{ autoarm.computed and autoarm.occupied_daytime_state == 'armed_home'}}"
    armed_away:
      conditions: "{{ not autoarm.occupied and autoarm.computed}}"
    disarmed:
      conditions:
       - "{{ autoarm.occupied and not autoarm.night }}"
       - "{{ autoarm.computed and autoarm.occupied_daytime_state == 'disarmed'}}"
    armed_night:
      conditions: "{{ autoarm.occupied and autoarm.night and autoarm.computed }}"
    pending:
      conditions:
  # UI: calendar entities and calendar end modes are configurable via Options
  # state_patterns and poll_interval are copied into the Options the first time, and set there from then on
  calendar_control:
    calendars:
      - entity_id: calendar.alarm_control
        alias: Local Calendar only used for autoarm
        poll_interval: 60
        state_patterns:
          disarmed:
            - Disarmed
      - entity_id: calendar.family_events
        poll_interval: 300
        state_patterns:
          armed_vacation:
            - Holiday.*
            - Camping Trip.*
          armed_away:
            - Working at Office

  # MIGRATED buttons are copied into the UI options on first start, and can then be removed from here
  buttons:
    reset:
      entity_id: binary_sensor.button_right
    armed_away:
      delay_time: 180
      entity_id:
        - binary_sensor.button_right
        - binary_sensor.back_door_away
    disarmed:
      entity_id: binary_sensor.button_middle

  # MIGRATED copied into the Options the first time, and set there from then on
  rate_limit:
    max_calls: 5
    period: 60

  # DEPRECATED replaced by deeper Supernotify integration, set up in the Notifications section of the Options,
  # and will be removed when Home Assistant 2027.4 is released
  notify:
    common:
      data:
        actions:
          - action: ALARM_PANEL_DISARM
            title: Disarm Alarm Panel
            icon: sfsymbols:bell.slash
          - action: ALARM_PANEL_RESET
            title: Reset Alarm Panel
            icon: sfsymbols:bell
          - action: ALARM_PANEL_AWAY
            title: Arm Alarm Panel for Going Away
            icon: sfsymbols:airplane
    quiet:
      scenario: alarm_panel_quiet
      data:
        priority: low
    normal:
      scenario: alarm_panel
      source:
        - calendar
      state:
        - armed_away
        - armed_vacation
      data:
        priority: medium
```
# Help

# Troubleshooting

Source: https://autoarm.rhizomatics.org.uk/help/troubleshooting/

## Repair Issues

Auto Arm uses the Home Assistant repair system to report configuration problems:

- **Invalid Transition Condition**: A transition condition template failed validation. Check the condition syntax in your YAML.
- **YAML core configuration is deprecated**: Core settings have been migrated to the UI config entry. Remove the migrated keys from YAML (see the [Migration Guide](https://autoarm.rhizomatics.org.uk/configuration/migration/index.md)).
- **YAML notify configuration is deprecated**: The `notify` section has been replaced by deeper Supernotify integration in the options, and will be removed when Home Assistant 2027.4 is released. Move what is still needed to the **Notifications** section of the options, or to Supernotify scenarios, and remove it from YAML.

## Reload After YAML Changes

After modifying YAML configuration (transitions, buttons, notify, etc.), call the `autoarm.reload` service or restart Home Assistant for changes to take effect.

## Debug Logging

Enable debug logging for Auto Arm to see detailed operation logs:

```yaml
logger:
  logs:
    custom_components.autoarm: debug
```

All Auto Arm log messages use the `AUTOARM` prefix for easy filtering.

## Options

- [AI Agents](https://autoarm.rhizomatics.org.uk/help/ai_help/index.md) can give very good help these days, even the free one built into [Google Search](https://autoarm.rhizomatics.org.uk/help/ai_help/#google-and-ai-assisted-help).
- [Troubleshooting your configuration](https://www.home-assistant.io/docs/configuration/troubleshooting/) has the generic Home Assistant advice
- Auto Arm has a [Diagnostics](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/diagnostics/) bundle available from the integration page
- Have a look at the [What's New](https://autoarm.rhizomatics.org.uk/changelog/), including any breaking changes, and any of the known [Issues](https://github.com/rhizomatics/autoarm/issues) or [Support Discussions](https://github.com/rhizomatics/autoarm/discussions).
- Use the [Tools](https://www.home-assistant.io/docs/tools/dev-tools/) to call the action directly, listen to events, or view states
- Since Auto Arm manages Home Assistant contexts, you can see the entire history of a why an alarm state changed, what the original trigger was, and also downstream things notifications, all laid out in the state history
- Supernotify also has some of additional actions to `enquire_configuration`,`reload` configuration and `reset_state`, and offers lots of diagnostic entities

## Advanced Agent Usage

- If you have a desktop or coding agent, then giving it access to Home Assistant config make it much easier to resolve issues and correct config.
- Easiest way of doing that is with the [Samba Share](https://github.com/home-assistant/addons/tree/master/samba) app for Home Assistant.
- For example, on a Mac you can have the local `/Volumes/config` reading the main `\config` directory of Home Assistant.
- Caution is due where passwords and other secrets inside the Home Assistant directory could be exposed.
- The *Assist* integration also supports [MCP](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/mcp/) for queries
- For more advanced usage, the [Home Assistant REPL](https://autoarm.rhizomatics.org.uk/developer/ha_repl/index.md) developer shell can give easy agent access to the APIs, or deep access direct into the live internals and database with `live` mode. The latter is the sharpest tool available for agents.

# Known Limitations

Source: https://autoarm.rhizomatics.org.uk/help/known_limitations/

## Single Alarm Panel

Auto Arm supports only one alarm control panel per installation.

## YAML for Advanced Features

Everything needed is now migrated into Home Assistant's web based configuration settings. YAML configuration will be automatically migrated into the new visual config. Two things that remain YAML only are:

- Transition conditions (effectively the rules engine)
- Notification profiles (now deprecated)

## Calendar Polling

Calendar events are detected by polling, not real-time events. The default poll interval is 15 seconds per calendar. Very short calendar events (shorter than the poll interval) may be missed. This is a Home Assistant limitation, necessitated by the different styles of calendar supported, for example, Google Calendars.

## Manual Intervention Lock

When a manual intervention occurs (button press, mobile action, or alarm panel change), Auto Arm will not override the state until the next occupancy change or another manual intervention. This is by design, but can be surprising if you expect automatic state changes to resume immediately.

## Alarm Panel Compatibility

Auto Arm works with any entity that implements the `alarm_control_panel` domain. However, some panels may not support all alarm states (e.g., `armed_vacation` or `armed_custom_bypass`). When Auto Arm uses the panel's actions, as it does by default, an unsupported state is rejected by the panel, a warning is logged, and the panel is left as it was. Panels that need a code to arm or disarm can't be changed through their actions, since Auto Arm has no code to give.

## Python and Home Assistant Compatibility

The component automatically runs the entire test suite for the latest Home Assistant, and the 6 months old version, so that broad range of compatibility is maintained for the majority of Home Assistant users.

2026.2 was the last Home Assistant release to support Python 3.13. This has been supported for longer than the usual 6 months, however automated testing dropped with v2.0.0 of Auto Arm in October 2026. Auto Arm *may* continue to work with older releases, but it will no longer be assured.

If you can't move off Python 3.13 then don't upgrade Auto Arm to v2 or beyond.
